material.notes: Compared to Flutter (ref/flutter/material, IconButton standard/tonal/outlined): 40 x 40 circle at 1x in rest, hover, focus, disabled (Flutter 40 x 40, radius 20), halo and tonal fills within 3 levels (palette differs, see flutter-compare.md G4), outlined ring 1 px outline colour. Fixed: a focused outlined icon button kept a primary outline (turned #6e58a8); Flutter keeps the outline colour (#7f7a84 now). Pressed ripple and the hovered black outline in the refs are harness artifacts.
gaps: The sheet draws a control-kit Settings glyph (a rig has no loaded texture), so control.icon_button itself, which takes a texture, is not what is shown: examples/looks/icon_button.e builds it through e.ui.looks_a.icon_button_glyph
Linux shows the Adwaita edit-copy symbolic icon through button_with_svg, Material its own material_icon_button; neither is the Settings glyph of the other looks

Windows draws a guessed 32 x 24 box (no capture of a v3 or Windows 11 icon-only button); Windows dark places the glyph about 2 px low and right because the dark picture-button path assumes a caption beside it

material.notes: Compared to Flutter (radio rest/hover/focus/disabled/selected): halo 40 x 40 matches; ring is 20 x 20 against Flutter's 18 x 18 (M3 spec and Material Web say 20; recorded in flutter-compare.md). Focus layer colour differs from Flutter (see checkbox).
gaps: radio-checked-rest: the reference shows the dot growing (centre coverage 72.4 against 83.4 settled), ours is 79; 212 px over 12 levels in light, 215 in dark.

Text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model of android-text.md (hinted outline, six by five samples, ClearType boxes averaged to grey, Skia's pre-blend table), which is how the Chrome for Testing on Windows references are drawn: 93 to 96 % of text ink pixels are exact (every channel within 2 levels) on the Material sheets, the rest are anti-aliasing edges of single glyphs. A second mode, AndroidSkia (a device's Skia over FreeType), exists next to it for Android devices; no device capture exists to measure it against.

The error check box is the M3 error tokens applied to Material Web's element (the library defines them but draws no error state)
